subject: Request: streaming endpoint first-byte / sustained-rate variance for Nimbus POC
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: procurement@nimbushealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 08 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: streaming endpoint first-byte / sustained-rate variance for Nimbus POC

Hi Elaine / Nimbus procurement team,

Thanks again for the conversation earlier this week. As we prepare the POC for the clinical summarization flow, Nimbus has asked us to document an SLA variance for streaming endpoints that differs from our standard hosted guarantees. The two items they flagged are: time-to-first-token (TTFT) expectations and sustained tokens/sec on long-running streaming sessions (~10k token transcripts).

Attached: 20270508_sla-exception-proposal.pdf — a short proposal that outlines the ask and trade-offs. Also attaching our raw benchmark CSV for the model variant we expect to serve.

High-level ask from Nimbus: 100ms TTFT and sustained >= 250 tokens/sec for sustained sessions. Based on our current infra and the model they want (Quantized LlamaX-13B with 8k KV-cache), I don’t think we can meet 100ms TTFT consistently on hosted Dedicated nodes in us-west without either changing kernel choices or adding prefetching / pinned instances. Our likely achievable baseline is ~140–160ms TTFT with sustained ~220 tokens/sec in tests, with variance depending on sequence lengths.

Requesting internal sign-off to propose a formal variance to Nimbus: 1) commit to 150ms TTFT P95 (instead of 100ms) for the POC, 2) commit to sustained 220 tokens/sec P50 with a remediation credit schedule if we miss the P95 TTFT by >40ms on measured weekly windows.

If we can get legal and finance okay on the credit schedule, I’ll propose the variance to Nimbus and include the benchmarking doc/signed acceptance.

Next steps I propose:
- Karthik: quick note on technical mitigations and realistic numbers (can you confirm the infra numbers and whether a burst-cached node would tighten TTFT?)
- Marissa: lead commercial with Nimbus and propose the remediation credit language (simple % credit for missed P95 events)
- Priyom: are there any security/compliance blockers to running the pinned instance prototype for the POC?

Thanks — I’ll wait for internal alignment before sending a formal response.

Best,
Rishi
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

Attachments: 20270508_sla-exception-proposal.pdf, benchmark_streaming_v2.csv
From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@nimbushealth.com>

Cc: Ryan Cho <ryan.cho@nimbushealth.com>, procurement@nimbushealth.com
Date: Sat, 08 May 2027 13:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: streaming endpoint first-byte / sustained-rate variance for Nimbus POC

Thanks Rishi — appreciate the quick summary and the attachments. A few clarifying points from our side before we move forward: 

- The 100ms TTFT request comes from our UX team; it’s a hard requirement for the clinician-facing live view. If you can’t meet 100ms, we need to understand compensating SLAs (credits / fallbacks).
- The 250 tokens/sec is an averaged expectation across long calls; we can tolerate short dips but need the P50 to be in that ballpark.
- We’d like these commitments captured in an SOW addendum or an appendix to the MSA with clear measurement windows and an agreed data capture method.

Please let us know what Redwood can commit for the POC and what mitigation language you are proposing. Also confirm whether the pinned/burst option requires additional procurement commitments from our side (e.g., a reserved node).

Best,
Elaine
Director of Procurement, Nimbus Health

Hi Elaine — quick technical note from the infra side.

Summary of lab runs (see attached CSV link):
- Model: Quantized LlamaX-13B (8-bit / KV-8k) on A100-equivalent Dedicated nodes.
- TTFT (cold): median 120ms, P95 155ms. Cold runs include KV cache misses and kernel warm-up.
- TTFT (warm/prefetched): median 85ms, P95 110ms when we run a warm prefetch window and keep a pinned worker warm.
- Sustained tokens/sec: median 230 tps across 10k token sessions; P50 ~225 tps, occasional dips to ~180 tps when memory thrash occurs.

Interpretation: achieving 100ms P95 TTFT reliably without keeping a pinned warm worker is unrealistic. However, with a pinned warm worker (per-customer reserved instance or a small pool) we can get to ~110ms P95 with room to optimize kernel selection. The trade-off is cost (reserved capacity).

Options to propose to Nimbus:
A) Pinned warm instance for the POC: commit 110ms P95 TTFT and sustained 230 tps P50. Requires reserved node for the POC duration.
B) Shared capacity + remediation credits: commit 150ms P95 TTFT, 220 tps P50, with a weekly credit schedule if P95 > 190ms on measured windows.

I’ve uploaded the detailed CSV to our drive: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/benchmark_streaming_v2.csv — feel free to inspect.

-Karthik
Staff Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Looping in Priyom for compliance/ops input and flagging commercial next steps.

Suggested commercial language for the variance (high level):
- POC term (60 days): Option A (pinned warm instance) priced as a fixed monthly add-on OR Option B (shared) with a remediation schedule.
- Remediation: if TTFT P95 exceeds committed target by >40ms on a weekly measurement window, credit 10% of that week’s usage for the POC. For sustained-rate misses >30% of committed P50 for a week, credit 15% for that week.
- Measurement & reporting: Redwood will provide weekly measurement exports (CSV) and the HubSpot deal will link to a read-only benchmark report. Disputes escalated to a technical review within 3 business days.

Priyom — can you confirm whether the pinned instance approach requires any paperwork or security exceptions? If so we should list them in the SOW addendum.

If legal/finance approve the simple credit structure above I’m happy to present to Elaine and ask for a quick sign-off or DocuSign acknowledgement for the POC appendix.

Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Elaine — thanks for the quick back-and-forth. Internal alignment complete; summary below and next steps.

Proposal we’re presenting for the POC:
- Option A (recommended): Pinned warm instance for duration of 60-day POC. Commitments: TTFT P95 <= 110ms, sustained tokens/sec P50 >= 230. Pricing: fixed add-on fee for pinned node. No additional procurement needed beyond POC add-on; Redwood will surface the exact SKU in the SOW appendix.
- Option B (shared capacity): Commit TTFT P95 <= 150ms, sustained tokens/sec P50 >= 220. Remediation: weekly measurement windows, 10% credit if TTFT P95 > 190ms for that week; 15% credit if sustained P50 < 154 tps for that week.

We’ve prepared a short SOW addendum and a one-click acknowledgement via DocuSign if you’re comfortable. DocuSign preview: https://docusign.net/sign/NIM-EXCEPTION-2027. HubSpot deal updated: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/2314097/NIM-2027-0427. Benchmark data: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/benchmark_streaming_v2.csv

If you want to proceed with Option A, we’ll activate a pinned warm worker and share a kickoff checklist for the POC. If you prefer Option B, we’ll include the remediation language in the SOW addendum.

Can you confirm which option Nimbus prefers so we can route to DocuSign?

Thanks,
Rishi
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
